s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic perianal disease with recent worsening of symptoms and development of a perianal mass
salient_findings: Internal fistula opening at the dentate line
key_facts: 12-year history of perianal fistula
Recent onset of mucinous discharge
Pain and perianal induration
History of incision and drainage of a recurrent perianal abscess
Two indurated, ulcerative lesions each 7 cm in diameter
Three external fistula openings around the anus
No inguinal lymphadenopathy
Internal fistula opening at the right side of the dentate line
Normal mucosa in the rectum and colon on digital and endoscopic examination
Well-defined mass at the level of the anorectal junction extending into the right ischiorectal fossa
Enlarged pelvic lymph nodes
No inguinal nodal or distant metastases
Mucinous adenocarcinoma on histological examination
Serum carcinoembryonic antigen level within the normal range

shortlist.label: Anal gland carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic perianal disease with recent worsening of symptoms and development of a perianal mass

shortlist.label: Cloacogenic carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a well-defined mass at the anorectal junction and enlarged pelvic lymph nodes

shortlist.label: Adenocarcinoma of the rectum
shortlist.why_kept: Internal fistula opening at the right side of the dentate line and mass at the anorectal junction

shortlist.label: Perianal Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: 12-year history of perianal fistula and recent onset of mucinous discharge

raw.rationale: The presence of mucinous adenocarcinoma on histological examination, combined with the patient's symptoms and the location of the mass at the anorectal junction, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Anal gland carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific histological finding of mucinous adenocarcinoma and the clinical presentation more directly align with mucinous adenocarcinoma of the anus.

rejected.label: Cloacogenic carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor and the provided information does not specifically suggest this diagnosis over mucinous adenocarcinoma of the anus.

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma of the rectum
rejected.why: The mass is described at the level of the anorectal junction and extends into the ischiorectal fossa, but the primary site appears to be the anus given the clinical and histological findings.

rejected.label: Perianal Crohn's disease
rejected.why: The long history of perianal fistula could suggest Crohn's disease, but the recent onset of mucinous discharge, pain, and the histological finding of mucinous adenocarcinoma point away from this diagnosis.
